newsitem.title: UK: Airline insurer says IATA deal won't cut bills.
newsitem.headline: Airline insurer says IATA deal won't cut bills.

text.p: An international agreement aimed at removing limits on compensation for injuries in air accidents will not reduce insurance bills or stop manufacturers being sued, a leading underwriter said on Tuesday.

Tony Medniuk, head of the British Aviation Insurance Group, told an airline insurance conference the International Air Transport Association's intercarrier agreement which would end airline liability limits to passengers, will mean insurers could pay more.
"In my mind, the architects of unlimited liability have
either ignored or underestimated what will be a significant impact on claims handling," he said.
Medniuk said the agreement is supposed to lead to lower legal costs after air crashes, as plaintiffs will no longer have to waste time proving wilful misconduct to have liability limits set aside.
Proponents also argue that, as satisfaction for damages will be received from the airline, litigants will not need to sue manufacturers and other third parties.
"The agreement allows passengers to sue in the country they live in or have their country's law applied in a foreign court, " said Medniuk.

"I forsee a new kind of forum shopping evolving, and it is not difficult to anticipate a whole raft of new litigation as plaintiffs seek a favourable jurisdiction by reason of birth, adoption, marriage, tax presence,or whatever," he said.
Medniuk added that aircraft manufacturers would not
magically fall out of the litigation loop.
"There is considerable evidence to the contrary," he said.

"In the U.S., where unlimited liability for domestic flights has long been the case, there are numerous examples of manufacturers being brought into settlements from the moment an accident happens." he said.
